subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in provider-profile pool routing contract for batch/worker workloads, and what minimal public config and state surface should ship first?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, persisted auth state, provider fallback behavior, status/probe output, and upgrade defaults, so automation should not invent the product boundary or compatibility story.

options.title: Design Minimal Additive Core Pool Routing
options.body: Define one default-preserving opt-in pool contract, start with one observable strategy, and leave quota/bucket/weighting expansion behind later scoped work.

options.title: Keep This As The Broad Tracker
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate narrower open work on key buckets, same-provider rotation depth, model/auth binding, and pace-aware governance before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Plugin Or Sidecar Hooks
options.body: Keep current core behavior and only extend plugin/provider hooks if maintainers decide native pool routing is too broad for core right now.

recommendation.title: Design Minimal Additive Core Pool Routing
recommendation.body: Define one default-preserving opt-in pool contract, start with one observable strategy, and leave quota/bucket/weighting expansion behind later scoped work.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is the product/config contract across auth and provider routing, where steipete has the strongest sampled history among the likely owners.
